content: The diagnostic criteria for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) have been a subject of global discussion, with the International Association of Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups (IADPSG) criteria being widely recognized and adopted. These criteria, often referred to as the one-step screening strategy for GDM, have achieved international acceptance as the preferred approach for identifying GDM. However, comparative studies evaluating the one-step method against the traditional two-step method in terms of population-wide outcomes have yielded inconsistent findings. This variability highlights the need for further research and refinement to optimize screening strategies for GDM.
